name: Citizenship by Registration (Distinguished Public Service or Professional Eminence)

requirements.blocker_text: Must have rendered distinguished public service to Sri Lanka, or be a person of eminence in a profession, and be ordinarily resident in Sri Lanka.
No more than 25 persons may be registered as citizens under this provision in any one calendar year, nationwide across all applicants.

evidence_required.document: Evidence of distinguished public service or professional eminence
Proof of ordinary residence in Sri Lanka

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR-hosted legal database) -- Sri Lanka Citizenship Act No. 18 of 1948, Section 13: registration for persons who have rendered distinguished public service to Sri Lanka or are of professional eminence, ordinarily resident, capped at 25 registrations per calendar year

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Sri Lanka). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 sourcing only (see lk_citizenship_by_descent.json's notes). MOST STRUCTURALLY DISTINCTIVE FINDING IN THIS BUILD, WORTH STATING PLAINLY: this is the closest thing Sri Lanka's Citizenship Act has to ordinary residence-based naturalisation -- and it is not that at all. There is no general provision in the 1948 Act allowing an ordinary long-term foreign resident (with no Sri Lankan spouse, no distinguished public service, and no professional eminence) to naturalise as a citizen through years of lawful residence, the way nearly every other country built in this dataset provides. Section 13 instead offers a discretionary, merit-based registration explicitly capped at 25 people PER YEAR, NATIONWIDE, across every applicant in the country -- a hard numerical ceiling not seen in this exact form anywhere else in this dataset (contrast the DV Lottery-style numeric caps some countries use for a specific immigration category, versus this being the cap on the ENTIRE ordinary-citizenship-by-merit pathway for a nation of over 20 million people). application_window is populated here (cap_type: fixed_number) specifically to surface this cap structurally rather than bury it in prose alone; selection_odds is left null since no source in this build gave the annual applicant pool needed to compute an actual approval rate against the 25-person ceiling. Evidence difficulty for the underlying qualification is marked 'often_impossible' deliberately -- 'distinguished public service' or 'professional eminence' are not routine, demonstrable facts the way a residence period or salary figure is. A long-term foreign resident of Sri Lanka with no Sri Lankan spouse and no extraordinary distinction genuinely has no ordinary path to citizenship under the sources located in this build -- a real, disclosed structural gap, not an oversight in this build's research.
